The record:
Write the postmortem for the incident below.

Alert: HighLatency on io-shop
What the alert said [AL1]: p50 latency above threshold for 5m {A1}
Alert raised: 2026-11-12T01:43:00Z {alert_raised}
Nobody was paged: no on-call incident was linked to this one. An alert rule fires; a person is paged. Argus first posted about the incident in Slack at 2026-11-12T01:43:02Z {first_told}, and the document says so already: leave that post out, and do not say that no person was told. That nobody was paged is a finding of its own.
The alert rule waits 5 minutes {rule_waits} with its condition holding before it fires. The alert came within the 7 minutes 30 seconds {accounted_for} accounted for by its rule waiting 5 minutes {rule_waits} with its condition holding, its evaluation at intervals of 1 minute {rule_evaluated_every}, an unmeasured allowance of 30 seconds {scraping_allowance} for scraping and storing its samples and the whole minute the onset is measured to.
Broken from 2026-11-12T01:37:00Z {began} (the onset) to 2026-11-12T01:43:18Z {back_to_normal}, when the metrics show it back to normal.
That is 6 minutes 18 seconds {duration}, and every impact figure below is measured over that stretch.
Argus held the incident for 2 minutes 3 seconds {held}, until 2026-11-12T01:45:05Z {argus_stopped}. That is not how long the fault lasted, nor how long Argus went on working - leave it out of your answer.
The service's error rate over all its requests, before it began: 1.0% {errors_before}.
The same rate while it was broken: 0.8% {errors_while_broken}, peaking at 2.0% {errors_at_worst} - no higher than the worst minutes of stretches as long before it began.
Rise above baseline: none - no more of the traffic failed while it was broken than before it began.
The series behind the alert, `max(http_request_duration_seconds{quantile="0.5"}) * 1000` - its alert said "p50 latency above threshold for 5m {A1}" - which its alert rule evaluates and calls worse rising: 26.233333333333334 ms {series_before} before it began, 189.83333333333334 ms {series_while_broken} on average while it was broken, and 191 ms {series_at_worst} at its worst. Say what it measures in words, not by its query.
No rise in failed requests was measured, so the harm to report is what this series did: say what it meant for the people using the service, not that little or nothing failed.
Customer loss: none - the shop's takings over the incident fell short of the same hours whole weeks earlier by no more than those hours vary on their own, if at all.

What Argus did, in order:
  - [T1] 2026-11-12T01:43:02Z {T1.1} Argus: Received HighLatency on io-shop
  - [T2] 2026-11-12T01:43:03Z {T2.1} Argus: Moved the incident to INVESTIGATING - a worker took the incident up
  - [T3] 2026-11-12T01:43:03Z {T3.1} Argus: Called in the Investigator Agent
  - [T4] 2026-11-12T01:43:04Z {T4.1} Investigator Agent: Asked for the service's per-minute metrics, anchored on 01:43 {T4.2}
  - [T5] 2026-11-12T01:43:04Z {T5.1} Investigator Agent: Read back 361 {T5.2} minutes of metrics
  - [T6] 2026-11-12T01:43:04Z {T6.1} Investigator Agent: Placed the start of the incident at 01:37 {T6.2}
  - [T7] 2026-11-12T01:43:04Z {T7.1} Investigator Agent: Recorded where the 3 {T7.2} replicas run - all on Tesla-V100-SXM2-16GB
  - [T8] 2026-11-12T01:43:09Z {T8.1} Investigator Agent: Asked for production change events - deploys and releases, and flag changes from the flag provider's history, the 1 {T8.2} day 1 {T8.3} minute before Nov 12 01:38 {T8.4}
  - [T9] 2026-11-12T01:43:09Z {T9.1} Investigator Agent: Read back 2 {T9.2} production changes
  - [T10] 2026-11-12T01:43:09Z {T10.1} Investigator Agent: Read the service register - the service calls io-pricing (internal, owned by checkout-platform), io-summary-cache (internal, owned by checkout-platform), io-pay (third-party, owned by IO Payments Ltd)
  - [T11] 2026-11-12T01:43:09Z {T11.1} Investigator Agent: Read how far the deployment had rolled out - all 3 {T11.2} replicas run revision 0d8e826225f0de73958a8a8dd3d867b2ae249e72, deployed at 01:36:39 {T11.3}
  - [T12] 2026-11-12T01:43:12Z {T12.1} Investigator Agent: Read what the deployment of 0d8e826225f0de73958a8a8dd3d867b2ae249e72 changed
  - [T13] 2026-11-12T01:43:12Z {T13.1} Investigator Agent: Asked for the service's log lines, the 8 {T13.2} minutes before 01:43 {T13.3}
  - [T14] 2026-11-12T01:43:12Z {T14.1} Investigator Agent: Read back 28 {T14.2} log lines
  - [T15] 2026-11-12T01:43:17Z {T15.1} Investigator Agent: Formed 1 {T15.2} candidate cause, best first: C1
  - [T16] 2026-11-12T01:43:17Z {T16.1} Investigator Agent: Read every channel available
  - [T17] 2026-11-12T01:43:17Z {T17.1} Argus: Read the flag provider's history - 0 {T17.2} flag changes by anyone but Argus, the 1 {T17.3} hour before 01:43:17 {T17.4}
  - [T18] 2026-11-12T01:43:18Z {T18.1} Argus: Moved the incident to MITIGATING to act on a candidate
  - [T19] 2026-11-12T01:43:18Z {T19.1} Argus: Called in the Mitigation Agent
  - [T20] 2026-11-12T01:43:18Z {T20.1} Mitigation Agent: Rolled back the deployment of io-shop for C1
  - [T21] 2026-11-12T01:43:21Z {T21.1} Mitigation Agent: Waiting to see whether the service is still at the incident's level, from 01:44 {T21.2} - up to 161s {T21.3}
  - [T22] 2026-11-12T01:45:05Z {T22.1} Mitigation Agent: Looked at the service - no longer at the incident's level since 01:43 {T22.2}
  - [T23] 2026-11-12T01:45:05Z {T23.1} Mitigation Agent: Judged the action CONFIRMED
  - [T24] 2026-11-12T01:45:05Z {T24.1} Argus: Moved the incident to MITIGATED - rolled [io-shop] back off revision [0d8e826225f0de73958a8a8dd3d867b2ae249e72] and the rule that fired stopped firing
  - [T25] 2026-11-12T01:45:59Z {T25.1} Code-Fix Agent: Proposed a fix as a draft pull request - https://github.com/ohadraz/Argus-Demo-Target-App/pull/566

Changes to production it read:
  - [P1] 2026-11-11T21:36:39Z {P1.1} deploy 544cef36a8eaf45c5b030c3d5c21473d8176cef3 by kuki: deployed revision 544cef36a8eaf45c5b030c3d5c21473d8176cef3 from the ohadraz/Argus-Demo-Target-App repository's deploy/ directory
  - [P2] 2026-11-12T01:36:39Z {P2.1} deploy 0d8e826225f0de73958a8a8dd3d867b2ae249e72 by kuki: deployed revision 0d8e826225f0de73958a8a8dd3d867b2ae249e72 from the ohadraz/Argus-Demo-Target-App repository's deploy/ directory
  - Flags read, none came back.

Log lines it read, one per message:
  - [Gad41] INFO io-shop: account pages rendered normally - 2 {Gad41.1} occurrences in 3 {Gad41.2} minutes, 01:35–01:37 {Gad41.3}
  - [Gd3f7] ERROR io-shop: summary cache lookup failed - connection refused to redis://cache.io-shop.svc.cluster.local:6380 (# of 200 {Gd3f7.1} requests) - 8 {Gd3f7.2} occurrences in 8 {Gd3f7.3} minutes, 01:36–01:43 {Gd3f7.4}; # was 59 {Gd3f7.5} to 200 {Gd3f7.6}, typically 200 {Gd3f7.7}, highest at 01:37 {Gd3f7.8}
  - [G46bc] ERROR io-shop: account page request failed - ClientDisconnected: the shopper closed the connection - 11 {G46bc.1} occurrences in 8 {G46bc.2} minutes, 01:36–01:43 {G46bc.3}
  - [Gbac1] WARN io-shop: account page error rate at #% over the last minute - 7 {Gbac1.1} occurrences in 8 {Gbac1.2} minutes, 01:36–01:43 {Gbac1.3}; # was 0.50% {Gbac1.4} to 2.00% {Gbac1.5}, typically 1.00% {Gbac1.6}, highest at 01:41 {Gbac1.7}

Candidates it considered, in the Investigator's words - name them by their labels, but cite none; what they claim is not what happened unless a row of the record shows it:
  - [C1] The deployment of 0d8e826225f0de73958a8a8dd3d867b2ae249e72 at 2026-11-12T01:36:39Z {C1.1} changed the summary cache port in deploy/values-production.yaml from 6379 {C1.2} to 6380 {C1.3}. Every cache lookup is now refused, so account pages render without the cached figure and p50 latency rose from about 26ms {C1.4} to about 190ms {C1.5}. The source code was not changed and the cache dependency itself is healthy. [config-induced-failure, confidence 0.93 {C1.6}, confirmed]

Actions it took:
  - [M1] Rolled back the deployment of io-shop for [C1] (can be put back) - confirmed, still in place

What each deployment it looked into changed:
  - [D1] Deployment of revision 0d8e826225f0de73958a8a8dd3d867b2ae249e72 to io-shop, compared against 544cef36a8eaf45c5b030c3d5c21473d8176cef3 - the revision deployed before it.
      modified deploy/values-production.yaml
        @@ -22,4 +22,4 @@ resources:
         # address is right.
         cache:
           host: cache.io-shop.svc.cluster.local
        -  port: 6379 {D1.1}
        +  port: 6380 {D1.2}
  - A file [D1] does not list is as it was at the revision [D1] compares against.

What Code-Fix read in the source and proposed, in Code-Fix's words - nothing ran its test or its fix, and what it claims is not what happened unless a row of the record shows it:
  - [F1] The fault is in deployment configuration. `deploy/values-production.yaml` sets `cache.port: 6380`. According to the investigation, the cache is healthy and listening on 6379 {F1.1}, which was the value before deploy 0d8e826, and every lookup to 6380 {F1.2} was refused. This patch puts `cache.port` back to 6379 {F1.3} and changes nothing else in the file or in the repository.
      
      No test is included. The repo's tests cover Python modules, and I can't confirm a YAML parser is installed to test this file. The way to check the fix is in production after the platform syncs it: the "connection refused to redis://cache.io-shop.svc.cluster.local:6380" lines should stop, the cache hit ratio should go back toward its normal level, and p50 latency should come back down.
  - Say what the files Code-Fix read do, with the conditions it gives - a default as a default, never as all it does - and no wider: 'nothing in the files it read', never 'nothing in the code'. [F1] names revision 0d8e826 and [D1] is that revision's own diff - say what it shows rather than ask for it to be checked.

What ran, read at the revision running when the alert fired:
  - [S1] deploy/values-production.yaml at 0d8e826
      # Deployment configuration for the io-shop account service, production.
      #
      # Rendered into the cluster as a ConfigMap and mounted into the pod, which is
      # why the service reads this file rather than being handed environment
      # variables: the values here are the deployment's, not the code's, and changing
      # one is a change to configuration that ships without the service being rebuilt.
      #
      # Owned by whoever runs the shop. Changes here go out the way any other change
      # goes out - reviewed, merged, and synced by the platform - and land without a
      # single line of io-shop's source being touched.
      
      replicas: 3 {S1.1}
      
      resources:
        memoryLimitMiB: 2048 {S1.2}
      
      # Where the rendered-summary cache lives.
      #
      # The account page reads this cache before it works a shopper's spend figure
      # out, and recomputes when the cache has nothing or cannot be reached. So the
      # shop stays correct whatever is written here - it only stays *fast* while the
      # address is right.
      cache:
        host: cache.io-shop.svc.cluster.local
        port: 6380 {S1.3}
      

Action items the record already holds:
  - AI-1 (mitigate, done): Rolled back the deployment of io-shop
  - AI-2 (prevent, open): Review and merge the proposed fix
  - AI-3 (mitigate, open): Turn automatic sync of io-shop back on once its repository says what should run - until then nothing merged reaches it, and turned on sooner it puts back what the repository says, undoing what Argus changed by hand
PR #566 is a draft Argus opened for a person to review and merge. The record holds nothing about it after that: do not say it was reviewed, approved or merged, or that it was not - nor that the record holds nothing, which the document says itself. Nothing ran its test or its fix: say what it proposes, not that it corrects anything.
The document already states what set it off, in a section of its own: the change [P2].

Cite evidence in causal_chain by its label. In a contributing factor's addressed_by, name the record's own action items that answer it, by their number; an item you propose names the factors it answers in its answers, by their labels.

Call submit_postmortem with your answer.

The document, by field:
root_cause: The deployment configuration's summary cache port was changed from {D1.1} to {D1.2}. Nothing on the cache host accepted connections on the new port, so every cache lookup was refused. The account page handles an unreachable cache by working each shopper's spend figure out again from scratch, so pages stayed correct but became slow.
cause_in_plain_words: A configuration change pointed the shop's account pages at an address where their cache could not be reached, so every page had to work its figures out from scratch, which kept the pages correct but made them slow.
still_at_risk: The repository still sets the cache port that refused every lookup, so syncing the repository back into production before a fix is merged could slow account pages again.
symptom: Shoppers' account pages loaded slowly
causal_chain 1: Shoppers' account pages loaded slowly. The typical (median) time io-shop took to answer a request rose well above its usual level and stayed there, while no more requests failed than usual. (cites AL1; T6, under "What Argus did, in order")
causal_chain 2: Account pages could not use the rendered-summary cache. Every lookup to it was refused, so the page fell back to working each shopper's spend figure out again on each request, which is the slow path. (cites Gd3f7, under "Log lines it read, one per message"; S1, under "What ran, read at the revision running when the alert fired")
causal_chain 3: The lookups went to a new cache port. Deploy P2 at {P2.1} changed the cache port in deploy/values-production.yaml from {D1.1} to {D1.2} and changed nothing else. As of {T11.1}, all {T11.2} replicas were running that revision. (cites P2, under "Changes to production it read"; D1, under "What each deployment it looked into changed"; T11, under "What Argus did, in order"; S1, under "What ran, read at the revision running when the alert fired")
causal_chain 3 ruled_out 1: The earlier deploy P1 of revision 544cef3: metrics read back over the hours before the onset show the service healthy with it in place until the onset, and rolling back to it put the service back to normal. (cites T5, under "What Argus did, in order"; T6, under "What Argus did, in order"; M1, under "Actions it took"; T23, under "What Argus did, in order")
causal_chain 3 ruled_out 3: A change to io-shop's source code: the deploy's diff changes only deploy/values-production.yaml. (cites D1, under "What each deployment it looked into changed")
causal_chain 4: The change broke the service because nothing accepted connections on the new port, while the old port had served account pages normally. (cites Gd3f7, under "Log lines it read, one per message"; Gad41, under "Log lines it read, one per message"; D1, under "What each deployment it looked into changed")
contributing_factors 1: No check was seen, in review or before the deploy, that the cache address in the deployment configuration accepts connections in production.
contributing_factors 1 had_it_been_otherwise: The port change would have been caught before it reached production, and account pages would not have slowed.
contributing_factors 2: No check was seen during the rollout that new replicas could reach the summary cache, so all replicas moved to the revision that could not reach it.
contributing_factors 2 had_it_been_otherwise: The rollout would have stopped with the previous revision still serving, and the slowdown would have been held back or cut short.
contributing_factors 3: No alert on refused summary cache lookups was seen. The fault was found only by the latency alert, whose rule waits with its condition holding before it fires.
contributing_factors 3 had_it_been_otherwise: The refused lookups, logged from the minute of the deploy, could have raised an alert sooner, and the rollback would have come sooner.
action_items 1: Add a pre-deploy check that the summary cache host and port in deploy/values-production.yaml accept connections in the production cluster, and block the deploy if they do not.
action_items 2: Make io-shop's rollout stop when new replicas cannot connect to the summary cache at startup, leaving the previous revision serving.
action_items 3: Add an alert on io-shop's summary cache lookup failures (refused connections) and cache hit ratio.
action_items 4: Link the HighLatency alert on io-shop to an on-call rotation so that a person is paged when it fires.
went_wrong 1: Nobody was paged: the alert was linked to no on-call incident, so no person was brought in while production was slow.

Not to be judged:
  - Names in braces, such as {T5.1} or {duration}, are figures code writes in from the row they name. They are not judged.
  - Action items propose what to do; they make no claim about the record.
  - Whether something went well, went wrong or was lucky is a judgement. Only a fact it states is judged, and whether a went_wrong item is one its field excludes.

Judge every claim in the document, and answer by calling judge_claims.

tools.description: Submit every claim in the document, each either as supported or as flagged. Supported: the document's own words, quoted exactly, and the record's rows that support it. Flagged: the document's own words, quoted exactly, why, and the record's rows that contradict it (none where no row speaks to it at all). Empty lists say the document makes no claim to judge.

why.description: One sentence: what the record holds instead. Never empty.

tools.name: judge_claims
